channel.title: Personal News Feed — News & World Affairs
channel.description: Personally scored news, world affairs, opinion/analysis & foreign affairs, business & finance, and San Diego/local articles curated by news-filter

item.title: Rhysida ransomware group claims responsibility for cyberattack on El Cajon data
item.description:
Source: NBC 7 San Diego Original headline: Suspected cyberattack targets city of El Cajon
The city of El Cajon experienced a network security incident on Sept. 27, potentially exposing sensitive health data, financial information, and undercover police rosters. A nearly eight-terabyte trove of data, including employee W-2s and 911 call recordings, appeared on a ransomware leak site. The Rhysida ransomware group has claimed responsibility for the theft. City Manager Graham Mitchell confirmed that an internal investigation is underway and a third-party forensic firm has been hired to determine the scope of the event. Mitchell stated that the city remains fully operational and is focused on a safe remediation process to protect maintained data. Cybersecurity expert Gary Hayslip, formerly with the City of San Diego, noted that criminal syndicates view data as a multi-billion dollar business and that cities are ripe targets due to their intricate environments and mix of old and new technologies. Hayslip encouraged other county cities to shore up defenses and utilize available resources to prevent similar vulnerabilities.

item.title: Multiple fires damage IMS Recycling Center in Barrio Logan
item.description:
Source: NBC 7 San Diego Original headline: Fire at recycling facility in Barrio Logan neighborhood knocked down
A two-alarm fire broke out at the IMS Recycling Center in the Barrio Logan neighborhood at 10:35 a.m. Tuesday. The fire involved multiple blazes that spread through stacks of cardboard and a loader truck. San Diego Fire-Rescue Department spokeswoman Candace Hadley said the fire created a smoke plume widely visible from Interstate 5. While the exact cause remains unclear, spokesman Jose Ysea said an initial report indicated machinery caught fire. More than 65 personnel responded to the scene, including the National City and Coronado fire departments. The Bomb Squad used a drone equipped with thermal imaging cameras to locate remaining hot spots. No injuries were reported, and workers evacuated the facility before crews arrived. The fire was mostly knocked down by 11:51 a.m., though extensive overhaul operations continued into the afternoon. To manage traffic, the California Highway Patrol shut down the 28th Street off-ramp from southbound Interstate 5, and Boston Avenue was closed between 27th and 28th streets. Both the highway exit and the road reopened to traffic around 2:30 p.m.

item.title: San Diego County reopens several Imperial Beach shorelines after meeting health standards
item.description:
Source: NBC 7 San Diego Original headline: Several beach areas in Imperial Beach reopened
San Diego County's Department of Environmental Health and Quality announced Monday that several shorelines in or near Imperial Beach have reopened after water samples met state health standards. Closures have been lifted for the Silver Strand shoreline, the Imperial Beach Pier, and stretches of Imperial Beach near Carnation and Cortez avenues. However, certain areas remain closed due to sewage contamination, including San Diego River Dog Beach and stretches of beach near the Tijuana Slough and the end of Seacoast Drive. Advisories remain in effect for La Jolla Children's Pool, La Jolla Cove, San Dieguito River Outlet, Tecolote Shores, Tourmaline Surf Park, and the stretch of beach near Marine Street. Residents can access information on beach advisories and closures through the County of San Diego or by calling a 24-hour hotline at 619-338-2073.

item.title: Hera spacecraft images reveal large crater on asteroid Dimorphos after impact
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater
First images from the European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft reveal a stadium-sized crater on the asteroid Dimorphos, caused by a 2022 impact from a Nasa spacecraft named Dart. The collision, which occurred at 14,000mph, successfully altered the asteroid's orbit, reducing its orbital period around the larger asteroid Didymos by approximately 33 minutes. Dr. Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist on the Hera team, noted the crater is almost as large as the body itself and that Dimorphos is now tumbling chaotically. Hera's mission is to assess the crash site and measure Dimorphos's mass to better predict how to deflect future space rocks. Mission team member Naomi Murdoch reported that images show boulders as large as 10m sitting on Didymos, a world with gravity 40,000 times weaker than Earth's. The spacecraft must navigate a field of hundreds of smaller boulders surrounding the asteroid pair. This research supports long-term efforts to track and defend against potentially hazardous objects, such as the upcoming study of the asteroid Apophis.

item.title: San Diego County officials urge vaccination as mpox cases increase
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego, San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: San Diego County Officials Urge Vaccination as Mpox Cases Double
San Diego County public health officials urge residents to receive the two-dose JYNNEOS vaccine following a surge in mpox cases. Since October 1, the county has reported 45 cases, representing more than half of the 77 cases reported so far in 2026. At this pace, 2026 could become the region's highest mpox year since 2022. While officials state this does not constitute an outbreak, reports indicate more than two-thirds of recent cases involved unvaccinated individuals. Of 16 cases reported since October, 10 occurred in unvaccinated people. There have been 13 hospitalizations this year, including 11 since July, though no deaths have been reported. Countyget health officials note that Clade I, which has circulated in California since 2025, was first identified locally in July. "Most local cases involve community transmission among unvaccinated and partially vaccinated individuals," said County Public Health Officer Dr. Sayone Thihalolipavan. "Vaccination remains one of our most effective tools for preventing severe illness and limiting the spread of mpox."
item.source: ABC 10News San Diego, San Diego Union-Tribune

item.title: Bank of Korea raises interest rate to 3.25 per cent amid chip boom
item.description:
Source: FT World Original headline: Bank of Korea raises interest rates amid AI chip boom
The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.25 per cent on Thursday. This marks the third increase this year under Governor Shin Hyun-song. Five of the seven Monetary Policy Board members voted for the hike, while two voted to hold. The decision follows inflation remaining at 2.8 per cent, above the bank's 2 per cent target. The central bank upgraded its GDP growth forecast for this year to 3.9 per cent, up from 3.3 per cent, citing a semiconductor boom. The bank expects chip demand to push the current account surplus to $500bn this year. Governor Shin noted that semiconductor operating profits account for one-fifth of national income. However, KB Securities' Peter Kim warned that a potential semiconductor cycle peak and a stock market collapse could limit organic growth. A dot plot released with the decision suggested further tightening may occur, with some committee members projecting a rate of 3.75 per cent in six months.

item.title: AI identifies author of 1808 travel sketchbook in 22 minutes
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: A historian says AI solved a 200-year-old mystery in just 22 minutes
Historian Mark Humphries used OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra to identify the anonymous author of an 1808 travel sketchbook in 22 minutes. The sketchbook, held at Yale's Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, contained few dates and limited captions. By analyzing primary sources like a fur trader's dinner diary and meeting minutes, the AI identified Louis-Guy-Charles-Guillaume de Rohan-Chabot, vicomte de Chabot, as the likely author. Humphries confirmed the finding by matching the sketchbook's content to a diary kept by Chabot, which contained a specific description of a sketch of Fort St. Joseph that matched a drawing in the sketchbook. While a human could perform this investigation, Humphries noted that the AI could check hundreds of potential candidates far faster than a person. Despite OpenAI president Greg Brockman celebrating the solution to a "significant historical mystery," Humphries remains cautious, noting that there are real limitations to the technology and that he does not use AI for tasks like writing.

item.title: Preparations reduce flood damage in Sunset Beach during high tides
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Sunset Beach's fortifications against El Niño lessen flood damage, officials say
High tides of 8.3 feet hit Sunset Beach on Wednesday, causing multiple homes to flood and water to breach seawalls, docks, and boat pilings. Despite the high water, Huntington Beach Fire Chief Eric McCoy said the city experienced less damage than in October because residents and public works crews took significant preventative measures. These efforts included sandbagging seawalls and placing ladders in drains. Sunset Beach Community Assn. president Tony Nobles said volunteers helped secure 35 homes and five businesses with sandbag walls. Resident Gary Scott, who previously suffered extensive damage in October, successfully protected his ground floor this time by installing a new retaining wall and a wall of sandbags covered in plastic. While some areas saw damage, McCoy noted that everything held up well, though he warned that tides could potentially rise even higher on Thursday. Nearby, coastal areas saw record-breaking or near-record tides, including 8.11 feet in La Jolla and 8.21 feet in Santa Barbara.

item.title: EU leaders meet to discuss long-term budget, Ukraine funding, and ECB leadership
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: EU leaders seek agreement on long-term budget and Ukraine at summit
European Council President Antonio Costa has called on EU leaders to reach a compromise on a long-term budget proposal for 2028-2034 during a two-day summit in Brussels. The proposed budget, which could reach nearly €1.6 trillion, may include a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member state contributions, though France has rejected the plan as inadequate. Costa stated the budget must be able to fund priorities such as security, defense, housing, and energy, while keeping national contributions at a reasonable level. The summit will also address Ukraine's financial needs for 2027 and beyond, building on existing support packages. Additionally, Eurozone leaders will discuss replacing European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, who intends to step down on February 7, 2027. Spanish candidate Pablo Hernandez de Cos is expected to receive backing for the presidency, facing competition from Klaas Knot. Other nominations for executive board positions include Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier.

item.title: Education Department error mistakenly enrolls certain student-loan borrowers in ineligible repayment plan
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Student-loan borrowers are being notified they’re ineligible for their income-based payments
An Education Department error mistakenly enrolled fewer than 0.1% of student-loan borrowers in a newer, more generous income-based repayment (IBR) plan for which they do not qualify. Only borrowers with loans disbursed on or after July 1, 2014, are eligible for the plan requiring 10% of discretionary income and offering forgiveness after 20 years. Borrowers with loans disbursed before July 2014 qualify only for an older version requiring 15% of discretionary income and forgiveness after 25 years. Loan servicer MOHELA notified affected borrowers that they have 90 days to select a new plan or they will be moved to standard or tiered repayment plans, which typically involve higher monthly payments. While some borrowers fear this change could jeopardize progress toward Public Service Loan Forgiveness, a department spokesperson stated that switching plans should not directly affect PSLF progress. This error follows similar notices sent to borrowers enrolled in the Biden-era SAVE plan, which the Trump administration eliminated.

item.title: Ocean Beach Dog Beach remains closed due to sewage spill and high bacteria
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Dog Beach in Ocean Beach remains closed for nearly a week after sewage spill sends bacteria levels soaring
Dog Beach in Ocean Beach remains closed for nearly a week following a massive sewage spill caused by a mechanical failure in a sewage pipe project near Mission Trails Park. The failure, which occurred last Thursday, released 37,000 gallons of raw sewage into a nearby river and subsequently into the ocean. While one site on the beach has reopened, two other sites remain closed because Wednesday's water samples still showed bacterial levels above the safe threshold. To reopen the beach, the city requires two consecutive days of clean water samples from those remaining sites. County data indicates that Dog Beach has exceeded safe thresholds for enterococcus bacteria numerous times this year. Some pet owners continue to let their dogs swim despite the contamination, while others avoid the water to prevent illness. "We were looking at the signs and just decided that its not worth the risk of having the dogs swim in contaminated water and them possibly get sick," said visitor Sharon Wilson.

item.title: Rapid GDP growth and AI investment drive higher inflation
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Economy Original headline: Inflation is still hot, fueled in part by the AI boom
U.S. GDP grew at an annual rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, marking the fastest growth in three years. Nationwide chief economist Kathy Bostjancic attributes this robust growth to increased consumer spending and artificial intelligence investment spending. However, this rapid growth may be fueling inflation, which reached 3.8% for the 12 months ending in October. EY-Parthenon chief economist Greg Daco states that inflation is being driven by heavy AI investment, rising fuel prices, and President Trump's tariffs, noting that businesses are passing these costs on to customers. Bostjancic expects the Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point at its December meeting. While some investors anticipate another hike in January, Bostjancic notes that outcome depends on market volatility. She also questions whether the record amount of AI spending will yield a sufficient return on investment, warning that if AI gains unravel, companies may slow spending on data centers, potentially dampening consumer spending and slowing GDP growth.

item.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia
item.description:
Source: FT World Original headline: FirstFT: Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia
Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners to halt shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. Manufacturing partners such as Dell and Supermicro, which package Nvidia’s chips into servers, notified buyers in these four south-east Asian countries that orders will not be shipped, according to three people with knowledge of the matter. The halt occurs as the United States increases export controls to prevent China from accessing AI computing power. These south-east Asian nations have become preferred destinations for Chinese AI developers seeking advanced chips that face Washington's restrictions. It remains unclear if the shipment halt is temporary as Nvidia and its partners work to comply with new export controls. Separately, France and Germany are seeking to protect the next seven-year EU budget from a potential Marine Le Pen presidency, as the French leader has suggested halving her country's net contribution and ending funding for Ukraine.

item.title: San Diego International Airport expects million passengers during holiday travel period
item.description:
Source: NBC 7 San Diego, ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: San Diego International Airport Navigates Mixed Travel Conditions Ahead of Thanksgiving Holiday
San Diego International Airport faced mixed traffic conditions on Wednesday, with reports of varying delay extents. The FAA issued a ground delay until 3:59 p.m. due to increased demand, noting that departures to San Diego were delayed by an average of 27 minutes. While ABC 10News reported that conditions remained calm with no major delays exceeding 15 minutes, NBC 7 reporter Nicole Gomez noted growing TSA lines in Terminal 1 starting around 9 a.m. Public information officer Nicole Hall stated that delays in arriving flights can impact departing flights. The busy holiday travel period, running from Friday, November 20 through Monday, November 30, is expected to see close to a million passengers, an increase of 8 to 10 percent over last year. NBC 7 projects up to 100,000 passengers will pass through the airport this Sunday. On a national level, AAA expects nearly 6 million people will travel by air this holiday weekend.
item.source: NBC 7 San Diego, ABC 10News San Diego

item.title: Ukraine hits Russian military aircraft and oil refineries in long-range strikes
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
Ukraine damaged five Russian military aircraft in an attack on the Savasleyka airfield, located 300km east of Moscow. Kyiv's General Staff confirmed that three MiG-31s and two Su-34s were hit, though the full extent of the damage is still being assessed. The Savasleyka airfield hosts aircraft used to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs. Additionally, Kyiv reported hitting two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region, an area where Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said more than 145 drones were shot down overnight, leaving one person dead and causing power outages. Ukraine also struck a radar system and fuel and logistics depots in occupied territories. The Ukrainian defense ministry stated that targeting fuel and ammunition limits Moscow's ability to carry out strikes. While President Vladimir Putin called for tightened security at energy facilities, he argued that Russia has stabilized its domestic fuel market without critical damage and promised that Moscow would inevitably retaliate. Meanwhile, Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure have left thousands without power and killed ten people between 24 and 25 November.

item.title: Fuel truck crash and fire on Giza highway kills 31 people
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Egypt: At least 31 dead after fuel truck overturns on highway
A fuel tanker overturned on the Ring Road in the Waraq district of Giza, Egypt, on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people and injuring 21 others. The crash ignited a massive fire that charred at least 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles. Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar stated that 39 ambulances responded to the scene and that the death toll could rise. Rescue workers pulled victims from vehicles in the densely populated neighborhood, and investigators are using DNA tests to identify badly burned victims. Egypt's public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the crash. President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi directed authorities to provide support to the victims' families. International leaders, including Italian Foreign Affairs Minister Antonio Tajani and Algerian Ambassador Mohamed Sofiane Berrah, extended condolences to the Egyptian people. Frequent accidents in Egypt are often attributed to poor road conditions, reckless driving, and lax safety enforcement.

item.title: American Airlines flight diverted to Phoenix after passenger attempted to open exit door
item.description:
Source: NBC 7 San Diego, ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: American Airlines flight diverted to Phoenix after passenger attempted to open exit door mid-flight
American Airlines flight 1494, traveling from San Diego to Chicago, diverted to Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport Wednesday night after a passenger attempted to open the exit door at 35,000 feet. Air traffic controllers reported a "Level 3 threat" on board after the man refused instructions from crew members to return to his seat. Passenger Josh Flanders said it took approximately five minutes to restrain the man, who repeatedly said, "I’m not going to stop. I’m not going to stop." Flanders noted that some passengers, including military members, helped subdue him. The man sustained a minor injury and was transported to a hospital for evaluation, though no other passengers or crew members were injured. After landing around 1 a.m., law enforcement met the aircraft and took the man into custody, notifying the FBI. The remaining passengers deplaned and waited in Phoenix for approximately five hours while American Airlines secured a new crew to complete the trip to Chicago. Phoenix authorities say the incident remains under investigation.
item.source: NBC 7 San Diego, ABC 10News San Diego

item.title: Cannabis retailers offer holiday discounts as consumer spending shifts to way higher costs
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Business Original headline: In a time of rising costs, one Thanksgiving commodity is cheaper: cannabis
Cannabis retailers are offering steep discounts during the Thanksgiving holiday, a period known as "Green Week" or "Green Wednesday" that rivals 4/20 in sales and foot traffic. While travel and food costs rise, cannabis prices are declining due to a heavy discount culture. Beau Whitney, founder and chief economist at Whitney Economics, says these lower prices benefit consumer affordability but hurt operators. Whitney notes that as inflation rises, consumers are using holiday discounts to offset the costs of essentials like gas and groceries rather than increasing their total cannabis spending. This shift contributed to a revenue dip in 2025, the first such decline since 2014, caused by an oversupply of product. Although the industry saw a 5% sales increase compared to last year, forecasts for late 2026 and 2027 remain modest. Meanwhile, the federal government recently reclassified medical cannabis to Schedule III, a category shared by drugs like Tylenol with codeine.

item.title: Foreign troop withdrawals and political disputes threaten stability in Somalia
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: As foreign troops withdraw from Somalia, could al-Shabab take over?
Somalia faces increasing instability as foreign troops begin withdrawing and political disputes threaten scheduled elections. Ugandan forces, the largest contingent of the 12,000-strong African Union mission, began withdrawing last month, with a full exit expected next year. Ethiopia also plans to withdraw nearly half of its 7,000-soldier contingent. Former deputy director of the National Security Agency Abdisalam Guleid warns that the withdrawal could lead to a Taliban-style takeover of Mogadishu, noting that authorities have become overly reliant on foreign protection. While Information Minister Abdifatah Qasim Mohamud argues Somali troops are prepared to assume responsibility, analysts note the military is under pressure from al-Shabab and clan-based militias. Financial pressures mount, as donor grants account for two-thirds of the planned $1.36bn budget for 2026, yet only 35% of expected annual aid had been received in the first nine months of this year. Additionally, a dispute over constitutional amendments has delayed direct elections, with the Supreme Court ordering a roadmap within 30 days following a presidential term extension.

item.title: Almost 6 million Southern Californians expected to travel for Thanksgiving
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Nearly 6 million Southern Californians expected to hit the road for Thanksgiving holiday travel
AAA expects almost 6 million Southern Californians to travel by car this Thanksgiving holiday. While nationwide travel numbers are expected to be lower than last year, they remain above pre-pandemic levels. Travelers like Aaron Abrajano, who is traveling from Fallbrook to Escondido, anticipate heavy traffic on local roads and certain routes like the 805 South, particularly during rush hour. Gabryella DeSantiago, who is traveling to Temecula, noted the personal importance of the trip to see family after being homesick for several months. Despite the expected congestion on freeways and local roads, travelers continue to prepare for holidayget-togethers to spend time with loved ones.

item.title: Chris Kacher dies after falling from West Hollywood condo tower
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Man dead after plunging from multimillion-dollar condo tower in West Hollywood, authorities say
Chris Kacher, 58, died after falling from an 18th-floor unit at the Sierra Towers in West Hollywood. The Los Angeles County medical examiner’s office found Kacher’s body in the rear yard of the building, located on the 9200 block of Doheny Road. Authorities are investigating the death as a suicide. Lt. Chris Oakley of the Los Angeles County Sheriff Department’s homicide unit said Kacher, a resident of Beverly Hills, had requested to see an apartment in the building on Tuesday. While no one witnessed the fall, Kacher left behind a note that was recovered. Kacher was the son of Del Casher, the inventor of the wah-wah pedal. A resident with a doctorate in nuclear physics from UC Berkeley, Kacher described himself online as a composer and a "stock market wizard." The Sierra Towers is a 31-story building that has housed celebrities such as Cher and Robert Herjavec. Units in the building are valued at over $2.6 million for one-bedroom apartments and more than $4 million for two-bedroom units.

item.title: India urges US to resolve trade disputes through ongoing bilateral negotiations
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: India news: Resolve tariff concerns in trade talks — India tells US
India's commerce ministry has urged the United States to resolve trade disputes through ongoing negotiations for a bilateral trade deal. This follows a proposal by Washington to impose a 25% tariff on Indian goods, which could be reduced to 17% if a deal is reached. The move comes after the US Trade Representative announced new import duties of 20% to 40% on 14 trade partners to counter alleged excess industrial capacity. India rejected claims of having structural excess capacity in any sector. Meanwhile, India marked the 77th anniversary of the formal adoption of its Constitution. Prime Minister Narendra Modi called the document the "priceless heritage of Indian democracy" while criticizing the opposition as becoming "more of an obstructionist." Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi defended the Constitution as the "greatest weapon against injustice." Additionally, the Cockroach Janta Party, led by Abhijeet Dipke, planned a rally in Nagpur to protest alleged attempts by the government to dilute constitutional values.

item.title: Kim Jong Un urges wider use of tactical nuclear weapons during facility tour
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Kim Jong Un tours nuclear material sites, urges wider use of tactical nuclear weapons
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un toured nuclear material production factories and a research institute on Wednesday, calling for the wider use of tactical nuclear weapons. State media reported that Kim's visit included inspections of equipment such as uranium-enriching centrifuges and standardized tactical warheads like the Hwasan-31. Kim stated that North Korea's production capacity is steadily expanding and argued that tactical weapons must be used for different missions due to dangers from a hostile state on his border, referring to South Korea. He accused the United States of encouraging allies to seek nuclear-powered submarines and share nuclear weapons, calling the possession of nuclear weapons an irreversible choice. Kim warned that any attempt to deny North Korea's nuclear status, which was written into its constitution in 2023, would be treated as a declaration of war. Professor Lim Eul-chul of Kyungnam University noted the visit signals a strategy to raise the bar for future talks, moving toward a 'nuclear state versus nuclear state' basis. This visit marks Kim's fourth trip to a nuclear facility since September 2024.

item.title: India pledges $1.6 billion to Nepal as Prime Minister Shah visits New Delhi
item.description:
Source: FP Foreign Policy Original headline: Nepal’s New Leader Reaffirms Ties With India
Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah concluded a two-day visit to New Delhi on Monday, where Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a $1.6 billion assistance package for Kathmandu. Much of the aid is intended for reconstruction following August's floods. The two leaders pledged cooperation on satellite communications and urban development, and India announced it will open an Indian Institute of Technology campus in Nepal. This visit, Shah's first foreign trip, signals India's intent to maintain regional influence amid growing Chinese presence in Nepal. Meanwhile, former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announced she intends to return to Bangladesh on Dec. 16, the anniversary of the country's 1971 victory. However, Bangladeshi officials noted she remains a fugitive and requires a new passport, which the government has yet to issue. In Pakistan, senior opposition leaders Taimur Jhagra and two others from the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party were detained in Peshawar on Nov. 17. Jhagra, a former finance and health minister, remains in custody without details on his condition or location.
